name: Network Attacks & Analysis
tagline: Host discovery, port scanning, pivoting, packet capture, on-path interception, and network service auditing for understanding and testing traffic on networks you operate.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.desc: The reference network mapper: full- and half-open TCP/UDP scans, service/version detection, OS fingerprinting with -O, and a 600+ script engine (NSE) for targeted checks.
tools.when: Every assessment starts here — run a -sV service audit on hosts you own after a broad port sweep, then drill into specific services with scripts.

tools.name: masscan
tools.desc: Asynchronous TCP port scanner that sweeps entire CIDRs at line rate; its results pipe directly into Nmap or naabu for follow-up.
tools.when: Scan very large ranges fast — your whole lab estate or an entire /8 you operate — before focused Nmap work.

tools.name: RustScan
tools.desc: Rust port scanner that finds open ports across a /16-class range in seconds, then hands the results to Nmap automatically.
tools.when: Fast all-ports sweeps where speed beats verbosity; pair with -- -sV to keep Nmap's service-detection depth.

tools.name: naabu
tools.desc: ProjectDiscovery's fast SYN scanner focused on top-N port lists with parallel host/port batching; the port layer of the httpx/nuclei pipeline.
tools.when: Quick broad discovery feeding a recon pipeline: naabu --top-ports 1000 then export JSON to httpx.

tools.name: p0f
tools.desc: Passive OS fingerprinting via TCP/IP stack quirks (TTL, window size, DF) and HTTP signatures; needs no packets of its own, only observed traffic.
tools.when: Identify OSes on a network you operate without direct scans — feed it a capture or live traffic mirrored from your switch.

tools.name: nbtscan
tools.desc: Scans NetBIOS name services for hostnames, logged-in users, MAC addresses, and shared-disk hints across a Windows LAN.
tools.when: On an authorized Windows segment, census machine names and shares quickly when ICMP and ARP answers are filtered.

tools.name: Nmap NSE
tools.desc: Nmap's scripting engine ships 600+ community scripts (smb-*, ssl-*, dns-*, vuln-*) that interrogate services after a scan; run category- or name-filtered sets.
tools.when: After port discovery, run safe script categories (--script default,safe) or a specific script like smb-enum-shares against hosts you own.

tools.name: nmap-vulners
tools.desc: NSE script set that queries the Vulners API with detected CPE/service versions and annotates scan output with matching advisories and exploit links.
tools.when: Fast triage of version-fatigued service lists: run -sV --script vulners on your own hosts to surface known-CVE matches to patch.

tools.name: arp-scan
tools.desc: ARPs whole subnets and lists live hosts with MAC/OUI vendor — the most reliable L2 census, answered even where ICMP is filtered.
tools.when: First step on any network you operate: enumerate every physical host on the LAN before scanning services.

tools.name: netdiscover
tools.desc: Active and passive ARP discovery with a live table of IP, MAC, and vendor; passively learns hosts from traffic without sending a packet.
tools.when: A visual live view of your LAN, or passive L2 discovery when you want to stay quiet while monitoring your own segment.

tools.name: fping
tools.desc: Parallel ICMP pinger that sweeps ranges and prints alive/dead hosts in script-friendly output.
tools.when: Fast liveness check of large or off-subnet ranges where ARP-based tools cannot reach.

tools.name: massdns
tools.desc: High-performance DNS resolver that resolves and brute-forces huge name lists at tens of thousands of queries per second, emitting A/AAAA/CNAME results.
tools.when: Resolve or brute candidate subdomain lists on your own estate in minutes instead of hours of single-threaded dig.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/blechschmidt/massdns && cd massdns && make

tools.name: chisel
tools.desc: Single-binary TCP/UDP tunnel over HTTP(S) with reverse and SOCKS5 modes; one client, one server, no special privileges.
tools.when: Run a chisel client on a host you own and forward ports back through an HTTP egress that filters plain SOCKS.

tools.name: frp
tools.desc: Fast reverse proxy that exposes local services behind NAT via a public server; config-driven with TLS, auth, and load balancing.
tools.when: Stable exposure of lab services or a pivot point behind restrictive NAT you control.

tools.name: stowaway
tools.desc: Multi-hop proxy chain builder (agent/admin model) supporting TCP/UDP and dynamic forwards chained across several hops.
tools.when: Build long multi-hop chains across several hosts you control when a single tunnel is insufficient.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ph4ntonn/Stowaway && cd Stowaway/Client && go build

tools.name: rpivot
tools.desc: SOCKS4 reverse proxy: a client on an internal host you own connects out through your listening server, opening a tunnel into that internal network.
tools.when: When the internal host can egress only toward your server; lightweight Python, no agent install beyond the script.

tools.name: ligolo-ng
tools.desc: TUN-based tunneling: the agent builds an encrypted tunnel to your proxy, which routes full IP traffic into the agent's network as if you had a real VPN.
tools.when: Full network pivoting across a host you own — route arbitrary hosts/subnets without per-port forwarding.

tools.name: proxychains
tools.desc: Forces any TCP client through a chain of HTTP/SOCKS proxies by shimming its socket calls via LD_PRELOAD.
tools.when: Route existing CLIs through your tunnel(s) without rewriting them — proxychains nmap <target>.

tools.name: sshuttle
tools.desc: Transparent VPN over SSH that forwards arbitrary TCP/UDP/DNS for whole subnets through an SSH connection without per-port forwards.
tools.when: Pivot your whole routing table through a jump host you administer using just an SSH key.

tools.name: socat
tools.desc: Bidirectional relay between TCP, UDP, UNIX sockets, and files, with SSL and FORK support — the byte-plumbing workhorse.
tools.when: Expose or forward services between hosts, wrap TLS around a plaintext target, or daemonize a listener in controlled lab setups.

tools.name: Ncat
tools.desc: Nmap's netcat with TLS, proxy chaining, IPv6, and connection brokering built into a MIT-licensed binary.
tools.when: Read/write test a service, grab a banner, or relay a plaintext session without extra tooling.

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.desc: Graphical packet analyzer decoding hundreds of protocols with stream following, session reassembly, and deep dissection.
tools.when: Investigate a specific conversation or replay a .pcap from your network — the closest thing to seeing the bytes yourself.

tools.name: tshark
tools.desc: Wireshark's terminal sibling: captures and dissects live or file traffic with the full dissector set and JSON/CSV field output.
tools.when: Capture or parse on a headless host and pipe structured output into scripts.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.desc: Command-line packet capture with Berkeley Packet Filter expressions; the standard for headless and rolling capture.
tools.when: Capture on a server you administer or dump to files with -w for later analysis — trivially scriptable.

tools.name: tcpflow
tools.desc: Reassembles TCP sessions from captures into per-connection files, reconstructing transferred content instead of packet fragments.
tools.when: Pull actual payloads (files, HTTP bodies, plaintext credentials) out of a .pcap you own.

tools.name: bettercap
tools.desc: Modular MITM framework — ARP/DNS/DHCP spoofing, sniffing, HTTP proxies — with an interactive shell, caplets, and a REST API.
tools.when: Full-featured on-path testing on a network you operate: spoof, sniff, and log plaintext from clients you control.

tools.name: ettercap
tools.desc: Classic MITM suite with ARP poisoning, sniffing, filters, and plugin-based interception of plaintext protocols.
tools.when: Traditional LAN MITM lab work when you want the legacy plugin and filter ecosystem.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive HTTPS interception proxy with a terminal UI and Python addons for rewriting and scripting flows.
tools.when: Inspect or rewrite HTTP(S) from an app or device you control, with mitmproxy's CA explicitly trusted on that device.

tools.name: Responder
tools.desc: LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS poisoner that answers resolution queries on a segment you operate and logs the Net-NTLMv1/v2 hashes clients send to it.
tools.when: Validate whether your own Windows clients leak credentials when their resolver goes quiet — to justify disabling LLMNR/NBT-NS.

tools.name: mitm6
tools.desc: Poisons DNS via IPv6 router advertisements so Windows clients look up WPAD and other names through your server on the v6 network.
tools.when: Test IPv6 spoofing of your own dual-stack Windows clients to confirm mitigations (WPAD removal, RA filtering) are in place.

tools.name: hping3
tools.desc: Crafts custom TCP/UDP/ICMP packets via raw sockets with hand-tuned flags, timing, payloads, and fragmentation.
tools.when: Probe how your own firewalls treat malformed or flagged packets, or test a service on non-standard ports.

tools.name: Scapy
tools.desc: Python packet library for crafting, forging, and dissecting virtually any protocol; can send, sniff, capture, and fuzz from a REPL or scripts.
tools.when: Build bespoke probes or protocol fuzzers for your own services when off-the-shelf tools cannot express the exact packet.

tools.name: snmpwalk
tools.desc: Net-SNMP's tree walker: pulls entire OID subtrees (sysDescr, interfaces, processes, routing) when a community string is read-accessible.
tools.when: Dump as much SNMP-visible detail as possible from one of your managed devices using the read community after discovery.

tools.name: snmp-check
tools.desc: Perl enumerator that turns SNMP walks into human-readable reports — system, network, routing, and listening ports in one shot.
tools.when: Quick presentation-ready SNMP summary of a device you manage without memorizing OIDs.

tools.name: onesixtyone
tools.desc: Fast SNMP scanner that blasts sysDescr requests across a range with multiple community strings and logs responders.
tools.when: Discover which of your own network devices run SNMP with default or weak read communities across a whole estate.

tools.name: ldapsearch
tools.desc: OpenLDAP's query client: filters, attribute selection, base DN control, and search limits for directory interrogation.
tools.when: Query directory objects (users, groups, OUs, attributes) on a directory you administer or are authorized to audit.

tools.name: ldapdomaindump
tools.desc: Dumps Active Directory users, computers, groups, nested memberships, GPOs, and more from a single LDAP query with any valid account.
tools.when: One-shot AD network object dump for analysis and reporting during an authorized directory audit.

tools.name: smbclient
tools.desc: Samba's SMB/CIFS client for browsing, listing, and transferring files against Windows and Samba shares with full auth options.
tools.when: Test share access and anonymous or null listings on hosts you operate before deeper tooling.

tools.name: enum4linux-ng
tools.desc: Maintained Python successor to enum4linux; automates SMB/RPC null-session enumeration of users, shares, password policy, and sessions.
tools.when: Complete legacy SMB enumeration (users, shares, policy) in one command against an assessed host.

tools.name: NetExec
tools.desc: Successor to CrackMapExec: multi-protocol (SMB, LDAP, MSSQL, WinRM, RDP) credential-validated enumeration of shares, users, sessions, and policy across fleets.
tools.when: Credentialed health-check across many Windows hosts at once during an authorized assessment — who is admin where, which shares are open.

tools.name: Impacket
tools.desc: Fortra's Python implementations of Windows network protocols with ~100 example scripts — smbclient, secretsdump, psexec, wmiexec, getTGT, and more.
tools.when: Protocol-level SMB/RPC/directory work from Linux when you need scriptable, low-level control over the wire.

tools.name: showmount
tools.desc: Queries the NFS mount daemon for exported filesystems (showmount -e) on NFS servers, listing paths and export flags.
tools.when: Enumerate which NFS exports a host you operate offers, and with what flags — first step before any mount testing.

tools.name: rpcclient
tools.desc: Samba's RPC client that interrogates MS-RPC endpoints — user, domain, SID, and session lookups, often over null sessions.
tools.when: Legacy SMB/RPC enumeration (SID and user queries) when standard SMB clients are blocked on a network you're authorized to test.

tools.name: xfreerdp
tools.desc: FreeRDP's client: connects over RDP from the CLI with drive and clipboard forwarding, screenshots, and full NLA support.
tools.when: Access a Windows RDP host you manage for GUI testing, session capture, or share-mount tests.

tools.name: rdesktop
tools.desc: Veteran open-source RDP client with single-session support and configurable codec and bitmap options.
tools.when: Lightweight RDP client for older Windows services where FreeRDP is overkill.

tools.name: ssh-audit
tools.desc: Actively probes an SSH server and scores its configuration — kex, ciphers, MACs, key types — against known weaknesses and current advisories.
tools.when: Audit the SSH policy of your own hosts; ships CI-friendly JSON and HTML report output.

tools.name: lftp
tools.desc: Feature-rich FTP/FTPS/SFTP/HTTP client with mirroring, resuming, scripting, and batch transfers.
tools.when: Poke an FTP service you run: anonymous-login checks, recursive listing, and large recursive mirrors.
